$description: Loadout Studio tokens, W3C Design Tokens format (Community Group draft). Dark is the default value; every theme's value is under $extensions["studio.themes"]. Accents rebind color.accent, color.accent-text and color.on-accent. Spacing is multiplied by a density.

ground.$description: The page itself, behind everything. Text tokens are measured on it.

surface.$description: Panels that sit on the ground: dialogs, popovers, toasts, the palette, the widened side rail. In dark it is a shade above ground; in light it is white paper.

surface-2.$description: A second step up: the list row being hovered, a code block, a picked option's well, a meter's track.

scrim.$description: The dim laid over the page behind a dialog, the palette or the widened side rail. Decorative: the dialog itself carries the meaning.

ink-strong.$description: Titles, numbers and anything that must read first, on ground, surface and surface-2.

ink.$description: Body text and button labels on ground, surface and surface-2.

ink-soft.$description: Section labels (the spaced capitals of a zone heading) on ground, surface and surface-2.

muted.$description: Secondary text: notes, facts under a name, the 'why' line under a dialog title. On ground, surface and surface-2.

subtle.$description: Commands (`$ loadout …`), placeholders and timestamps. Still 4.5:1 or better (7:1 in high contrast) on every ground, because a command is read, not decoration.

rule.$description: Hairlines that only group things: the line after a zone heading, list separators. Decorative in dark and light; 3:1 or better in the high-contrast themes, where surfaces are set apart by borders.

control-edge.$description: The edge of a control that has no fill: an input, a toggle track, a segmented control. 3:1 or better on every ground in every theme.

focus.$description: The focus ring: a solid 2px outline, 2–4px off the control. 3:1 or better on every ground. White in dark, near-black in light, yellow and blue in high contrast.

moving.$description: Signal family Moving (working, running, doing, round running): the state glyph's ring, the orbiter, the meter fill. Also readable as text on every ground.

needs.$description: Signal family Needs (needs a decision, waiting for you): the glyph ring, the glow on whatever is waiting, an amber halo button. As text on every ground too.

needs-text.$description: Text that belongs to a Needs item: the question asked, the age of the wait. On ground, surface, surface-2 and needs-wash.

needs-wash.$description: The faint fill behind a card or toast that needs you. Never the only signal: the word, glyph and needs edge come with it.

bad.$description: Signal family Bad (failed, last round failed, blocked, limited): glyph ring and edge. As text on every ground too.

bad-text.$description: Text inside a problem toast or card. On ground, surface, surface-2 and bad-wash.

bad-wash.$description: The faint fill behind a problem toast or card, always with the word, the glyph and the bad edge.

good.$description: Signal family Good (done, met, accepted). Done and failed differ by glyph and word, never by this colour alone.

rest.$description: Signal family Rest (idle, open, captured, shaping, held, stopped, not attempted, unknown, dropped).

on-signal.$description: Text or a glyph drawn on a solid signal fill (the small glyph discs in the Ambient signal strip). 4.5:1 or better on all five families (7:1 in high contrast).

gauge.$description: The Gyroscope halo's spend ring and its legend dot. Always labelled 'Spend'; never a status.

shaping.$description: The Lens halo's Shaping ring and its mark. A stage colour on the halo only; as a state, shaping belongs to the Rest family. 3:1 or better on every ground.

line-1.$description: Map line 1's identity colour: its track, stops, badge and train. Identity, never state: a line keeps its colour from Captured to Done, and state is its Signal. 3:1 or better on every ground.

line-2.$description: Map line 2's identity colour: its track, stops, badge and train. Identity, never state: a line keeps its colour from Captured to Done, and state is its Signal. 3:1 or better on every ground.

line-3.$description: Map line 3's identity colour: its track, stops, badge and train. Identity, never state: a line keeps its colour from Captured to Done, and state is its Signal. 3:1 or better on every ground.

line-4.$description: Map line 4's identity colour: its track, stops, badge and train. Identity, never state: a line keeps its colour from Captured to Done, and state is its Signal. 3:1 or better on every ground.

line-5.$description: Map line 5's identity colour: its track, stops, badge and train. Identity, never state: a line keeps its colour from Captured to Done, and state is its Signal. 3:1 or better on every ground.

line-6.$description: Map line 6's identity colour: its track, stops, badge and train. Identity, never state: a line keeps its colour from Captured to Done, and state is its Signal. 3:1 or better on every ground.

line-7.$description: Map line 7's identity colour: its track, stops, badge and train. Identity, never state: a line keeps its colour from Captured to Done, and state is its Signal. 3:1 or better on every ground.

line-8.$description: Map line 8's identity colour: its track, stops, badge and train. Identity, never state: a line keeps its colour from Captured to Done, and state is its Signal. 3:1 or better on every ground.

on-line.$description: The number on a train and on a line badge, on any line colour. 4.5:1 or better on all eight (7:1 in high contrast).

term-bg.$description: The terminal's ground. The same as `surface` in Dark and Light, and `ground` in high contrast, so the terminal sits in Studio rather than on a slab of its own.

term-fg.$description: Default terminal text. 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

term-selection.$description: Selected text's background. Every terminal text colour stays 4.5:1 or better on it (7:1 in high contrast).

term-black.$description: ANSI black. In Dark and High contrast dark it is a background (term-fg reads on it); in the light themes it is text. Text colours are 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

term-red.$description: ANSI red: errors and removed lines. The same hue as `bad`. Text colours are 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

term-green.$description: ANSI green: success and added lines. The same hue as `good`. Text colours are 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

term-yellow.$description: ANSI yellow: warnings. The same hue as `needs`. Text colours are 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

term-blue.$description: ANSI blue: paths and links. The same hue as `moving`. Text colours are 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

term-magenta.$description: ANSI magenta. The same hue as `shaping`. Text colours are 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

term-cyan.$description: ANSI cyan. Studio's cyan, fixed: it does not follow the accent, because agents use it as a colour, not as Studio's accent. Text colours are 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

term-white.$description: ANSI white. In the light themes a dark grey, so it reads on white. Text colours are 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

term-bright-black.$description: ANSI bright black, the bold or emphasised form of term-black. 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

term-bright-red.$description: ANSI bright red, the bold or emphasised form of term-red. 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

term-bright-green.$description: ANSI bright green, the bold or emphasised form of term-green. 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

term-bright-yellow.$description: ANSI bright yellow, the bold or emphasised form of term-yellow. 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

term-bright-blue.$description: ANSI bright blue, the bold or emphasised form of term-blue. 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

term-bright-magenta.$description: ANSI bright magenta, the bold or emphasised form of term-magenta. 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

term-bright-cyan.$description: ANSI bright cyan, the bold or emphasised form of term-cyan. 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

term-bright-white.$description: ANSI bright white, the bold or emphasised form of term-white. 4.5:1 or better on term-bg and term-selection (7:1 in high contrast).

accent.$description: The accent in use. Cyan unless the person picks Ice, Magenta or Violet (`data-accent` on <html>, which rebinds this to accent-<name>). Rings, strokes, tab fills and every accent glow read it. The accent never means a state: state is the five signal families.

accent-text.$description: The accent in use, as text. Rebinds with `data-accent`.

on-accent.$description: Text on a solid `accent` fill. Rebinds with `data-accent`.

term-cursor.$description: The terminal's cursor: the accent in use, a block when the terminal has focus and an outline when it doesn't. The character under a block cursor is drawn in term-bg.

fill.$description: Cyan accent fill: halo rings, the tab fill, the current page's bar, the line after a zone heading. 3:1 or better on every ground. Read through `accent`, never directly.

text.$description: Cyan accent as text: zone numbers, links, the caret. 4.5:1 or better (7:1 in high contrast) on ground, surface and surface-2. Read through `accent-text`.

on.$description: Text on a solid Cyan accent fill (the WHAT SHOULD IT DO? tab). 4.5:1 or better (7:1 in high contrast). Read through `on-accent`.

fill.$description: Ice accent fill: halo rings, the tab fill, the current page's bar, the line after a zone heading. 3:1 or better on every ground. Read through `accent`, never directly.

text.$description: Ice accent as text: zone numbers, links, the caret. 4.5:1 or better (7:1 in high contrast) on ground, surface and surface-2. Read through `accent-text`.

on.$description: Text on a solid Ice accent fill (the WHAT SHOULD IT DO? tab). 4.5:1 or better (7:1 in high contrast). Read through `on-accent`.

fill.$description: Magenta accent fill: halo rings, the tab fill, the current page's bar, the line after a zone heading. 3:1 or better on every ground. Read through `accent`, never directly.

text.$description: Magenta accent as text: zone numbers, links, the caret. 4.5:1 or better (7:1 in high contrast) on ground, surface and surface-2. Read through `accent-text`.

on.$description: Text on a solid Magenta accent fill (the WHAT SHOULD IT DO? tab). 4.5:1 or better (7:1 in high contrast). Read through `on-accent`.

fill.$description: Violet accent fill: halo rings, the tab fill, the current page's bar, the line after a zone heading. 3:1 or better on every ground. Read through `accent`, never directly.

text.$description: Violet accent as text: zone numbers, links, the caret. 4.5:1 or better (7:1 in high contrast) on ground, surface and surface-2. Read through `accent-text`.

on.$description: Text on a solid Violet accent fill (the WHAT SHOULD IT DO? tab). 4.5:1 or better (7:1 in high contrast). Read through `on-accent`.

shadow-float.$description: Lifts what floats over the page (toasts, popovers, dialogs, the palette) off it. A soft dark shadow in Dark and Light; none in high contrast, where a 2px edge does the job.

density-compact.$description: Compact: more on the screen, for big monitors.

density-roomy.$description: Roomy: for touch, zoom and low vision.

density.$description: Set with data-density on <html>: compact, comfortable (default) or roomy.

space-1.$description: Between a glyph and its word inside a chip.

space-2.$description: Between a title and the facts under it; between stacked toasts.

space-3.$description: Between a halo ring and its label; inside a list row.

space-4.$description: The page's side gutter at 320px; padding inside a popover.

space-5.$description: Padding inside a toast and a palette row.

space-6.$description: The start rail's left padding; padding inside a dialog.

space-7.$description: Between a zone and the next; the page's side gutter on desktop.

space-8.$description: Above a page's first zone; around the Lens halo.

rail-width.$description: The side rail, collapsed. Pages start this far in. Not multiplied by density.

rail-width-open.$description: The side rail, widened; it slides over the page, it never pushes it.

control-sm.$description: Small halo buttons and chips. Never below 24px at any density (WCAG 2.2 target size).

space.$description: One scale, multiplied by the density in use: Compact 0.8, Comfortable 1 (the default), Roomy 1.25. Components read calc(var(--space-n) * var(--density)).

radius-none.$description: Panels, rails, the start rail, toasts, tabs: Studio is square. Shapes are carried by light, not corners.

radius-chip.$description: Signal marks and the small chips on a meter.

radius-pill.$description: Meter tracks and fills, the Lens/Map count pills.

radius-round.$description: Halo rings, glyph discs, orbiters: anything that is a ring.

glow-sm.$description: Blur of the glow on a glyph disc or the dot in a halo ring.

glow-md.$description: Blur of the glow round a halo ring and on a zone number.

glow-lg.$description: Blur of the glow on a hovered or focused halo ring, and the settle flash when something finishes.

glow-strength.$description: How much of the colour a glow carries in Dark.

tint-hover.$description: Accent mixed into the ground under a hovered row.

tint-picked.$description: Accent mixed into the ground at the start of a picked row's fade.

tint-line.$description: Accent mixed into a decorative hairline (the line after a zone heading).

glow.$description: Glow is light from the accent or a signal colour. It is on in Dark and off in Light and both high-contrast themes, where strokes and borders do the same job.

dur-instant.$description: Colour and text changes on hover.

dur-base.$description: A halo ring growing on hover, panels projecting in.

dur-slow.$description: A tether unfolding, the dim fading in.

dur-travel.$description: The Lens focus turning to a new item; a train between stops.

dur-breathe.$description: One breath of a Moving glyph. Loops only under full motion.

dur-toast-fold.$description: How long a toast stays open before folding to its small form.

duration.$description: Motion is set to full, reduced or none in Settings, and the operating system's reduced-motion preference always wins. Under reduced, things fade instead of travelling and nothing loops; under none, nothing animates.

ease-out.$description: Almost everything: quick out, long settle.

ease-travel.$description: Travel along a path: a train, the focus turning.

recede.$description: What is less urgent recedes to this when something needs you, and an idle signal dims to it. Dark only: text there stays 4.5:1 or better. In Light and both high-contrast themes nothing fades (a fade would break contrast), so the rise alone carries urgency.

z-ground.$description: Behind the page: the field map (FieldMap), which shows only where the page shows its ground.

z-page.$description: Things that float over the page itself but belong to it: a popover from a picker, the Next chip, a command line's suggestions.

z-rail.$description: The side rail at rest, and the Pages tab below 600px.

z-modebar.$description: The mode bar across the top.

z-focus.$description: Focus view, which starts below the mode bar and beside the rail.

z-rail-open.$description: The rail while it is widened, and the Pages slide-in with its dim. It draws over the mode bar and Focus view, which its dim covers like the rest of the page.

z-menu.$description: A menu opened from something on the page, such as a terminal tab's menu.

z-dialog.$description: A dialog, over its dim and over an open rail.

z-toast.$description: Toasts, over everything a person works in, dialogs included.

z-skip.$description: The skip link, when it has focus.

z-ambient.$description: Ambient view, which covers the whole screen.

layer.$description: The order of Studio's page-level layers, from the bottom up. Every z-index on something fixed to the screen, or on something that can overlap another region of it, uses one of these; a bare number is only for stacking inside one component, such as a badge over its card.

saira.$description: Saira, weights 100 900, normal. OFL-1.1; licence in fonts/.

jetbrains-mono.$description: JetBrains Mono, weights 100 800, normal. OFL-1.1; licence in fonts/.

display-xl.$description: Big numbers: a toggle's state in Halo controls, a dialog's result count.

display.$description: A page title and the Ambient corner numbers. Thin on purpose: the glow carries weight in dark; in light and high contrast the ink does.

title.$description: The thing in focus on Lens, a dialog's title.

ask.$description: A question waiting for you, where it is answered.

entry.$description: Text typed into the start-a-session rail.

body.$description: Body copy, list titles, toast text.

body-sm.$description: The 'why' line under a heading, legends, options.

label-zone.$description: Zone headings: spaced capitals, ink-soft, followed by an accent hairline.

label-tab.$description: The accent tab over the start rail, field labels, tab buttons.

label-nav.$description: Side-rail page names and the Lens/Map switch.

cmd.$description: The command beside or under every action that changes something.

mono-meta.$description: Times, ages and counts in feeds and meters.

mono-note.$description: Live counts under a page name in the rail, units on a meter.
